8 • MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOD
In 2025, MB’s brand value 
exceeded USD 2 billion, ranking 
among the Top 3 banks and 
Top 10 most valuable brands 
nationwide.
Dear 
Valued 
Shareholders, 
Investors, 
Partners, and Customers,
In 2025, the global economy faced multiple 
challenges 
from 
geopolitical 
instability. 
Amid such turbulence, Vietnam’s economy 
maintained a positive trajectory relative to other 
regional markets, with GDP growth reaching 
8.02%. Within the finance and banking sector, 
digital transformation created a vast space for 
development – expanding service coverage, 
optimizing efficiency, and improving customer 
experience – while also posing new challenges 
in cybersecurity and data protection. 
With strong determination and the support of 
regulators, shareholders, investors, partners, 
and customers, MB turned challenges into 
momentum, setting new records in 2025. Total 
assets exceeded VND 1.6 quadrillion (+43%) 
– the fastest growth among private banks. 
Profit increased nearly 19% to VND 34.268 
trillion. Credit outstanding crossed the VND 1 
quadrillion mark, rising 37% – a testament to 
MB’s commitment to fueling the nation’s growth, 
accompanying businesses and individuals, and 
key projects, and sustaining the financial system. 
The Current Account Savings Account (CASA) 
ratio remained around 36%, among the highest 
in the banking system, helping MB to reduce its 
cost of funds. With 35 million customers – mainly 
payroll and large corporate clients - MB built 
a stable, low-cost funding base. The cost-to-
income ratio (CIR) was maintained at 29%, below 
the industry average. Capital mobilization and 
credit growth accelerated; operational efficiency 
improved; ROE stayed strong and asset quality 
was well controlled. The non-performing loan 
(NPL) ratio was kept below 1.3%, meeting the 
planned target. These outcomes reflected MB’s 
focus on digital transformation, operational 
streamlining, and internal process optimization. 
In particular, 2025 witnessed clear progress in 
MB Group’s financial conglomerate model, as 
the Bank established a comprehensive digital 
financial ecosystem with eight subsidiaries 
operating efficiently across multiple business 
segments: banking (MBCambodia, MBV), fund 
management (MBCapital), securities (MBS), non-
life insurance (MIC), life insurance (MB Life), asset 
management and debt recovery (MBAMC), 
and consumer finance (Mcredit). In 2025, MB’s 
subsidiaries successfully fulfilled their assigned 
objectives 
and 
maintained 
their 
leading 
positions within their respective industries. 
The profit contribution from subsidiaries rose 
to 8.9%, clearly demonstrating the growing 
synergy across the Group and its joint efforts to 
MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOD • 9
Message from the Chairman 
of the BOD
create greater overall value for customers and 
for the nation. 
In 2025, MB’s brand value exceeded USD 2 
billion, ranking among the Top 3 banks and Top 
10 most valuable brands nationwide – a fivefold 
increase compared with five years earlier 
(according to Brand Finance’s ranking released 
on 15 January 2026). During the same year, MB 
contributed about VND 10 trillion to the State 
Budget, up 16% year-on-year, becoming one of 
the Top 5 banks with the largest contributions to 
national revenue. 
MB also remained a strong digital transformation 
pioneer, having fully accomplished its science, 
technology, and digitalization targets. As part 
of Vietnam’s Big 5, MB achieved remarkable 
milestones that reaffirmed its No. 1 market 
position in digital transformation, operating two 
major digital platforms – BIZ MBBank, serving 
over 358,000 corporate customers, and the App 
MBBank, serving the largest retail customer base 
nationwide with 35 million users. Supported by a 
standardized IT infrastructure and an attractive 
digital 
ecosystem, 
MB 
sustained 
steady 
customer growth year after year. Within five 
years, its customer base expanded thirteen-fold, 
a clear testament to the strength of MB’s digital 
strategy.
A new era of rising
In 2026, the macroeconomic environment will 
continue to offer promising growth opportunities, 
as Vietnam’s economy is expected to maintain 
strong momentum, with the Government 
targeting GDP growth of over 10% and GDP per 
capita exceeding USD 5,000. This will create a 
solid foundation for a critical period of national 
financial asset accumulation, providing ample 
room for the banking sector to expand. 
Seizing the momentum of this new era of rising, 
MB will focus on enhancing operational quality 
and strengthening resources for the 2026 – 2028 
growth phase. Accordingly, the Bank will adopt 
the 2026 action motto “Acceleration – Resilience 
– Efficiency” – Acceleration through technology 
and innovation; Resilience in every decision; and 
Efficiency through productivity, service quality, 
and the real value delivered to customers. MB’s 
strategy will continue to be rapid yet sustainable, 
expanding on a foundation of rigorous risk 
management and real-time data. In the coming 
phase, MB will prioritize improving capital 
efficiency, enhancing customer lifetime value, 
and maintaining its leading position in digital 
transformation – striving to become a Digital 
Enterprise, a Leading Financial Group. 
With its mission over three decades to deliver 
safety, convenience, and financial opportunity 
to Vietnamese people, MB will aim to welcome 
an additional 5 million new customers in 2026, 
bringing the total to 40 million customers, with 
deeper engagement through new platforms 
and services. 
During the 2026-2028 period, in line with the 
Government’s GDP growth objectives, the Group 
targets annual growth in outstanding credit and 
capital mobilization of approximately 30–35%, 
subject to the limits set by the SBV. At the same 
time, MB will implement synchronized initiatives 
to improve productivity and asset-quality 
management, while strengthening advanced 
governance mechanisms to maintain a return 
on equity (ROE) above 20%. The Bank aims to 
keep its NPL ratio below 1% in 2026 and below 
1.5% for the entire period, while continuing to 
maintain key performance indicators such as 
NIM, COF, ROA, and CIR among the leading 
banks in Vietnam.
In 2026, focus on key objectives: “Becoming 
Vietnam’s No.1 Digital Enterprise,” “Sustainable 
low-cost funding,” and “Efficiency and Safety.”
Accelerate the review and conclusion of the 
2022–2026 Strategy, while preparing to develop 
the next 3–5 year strategic plan.
• Strengthen direction and guidance for business 
units within the Bank and its subsidiaries to 
successfully achieve business targets and 
implement strategic initiatives. Enhance Group 
synergy to effectively leverage the ecosystem 
between MB and its subsidiaries, increasing 
their contribution to the Group’s revenue and 
profit. Subsidiaries will be guided toward ROE 
performance targeting approximately Top 3 
within their respective industries.
• Enhance governance standards, closely linking 
management effectiveness with sustainable 
growth, cost efficiency, and strict control of non-
performing loans to ensure the achievement of 
key business plans. Investment activities will be 
carefully managed, and investment budgets 
optimized to ensure effective risk management 
and financial efficiency.
• Stabilize the shareholder structure and 
strengthen corporate value, while improving 
management quality and refining governance 
and operational regulations in compliance 
with current legal requirements and advanced 
practices.
• Investment planning and enhancement of 
network efficiency: Continue identifying and 
investing in headquarters in the Southern,

Central, and other high-potential regions; 
further complete the network system across 
localities, regions, and potential international 
markets in alignment with business strategy; 
and strengthen coordination with Group entities 
to enhance brand presence and visibility.
• Accelerate technology adoption to enhance 
customer experience and improve productivity 
across the Group by 20% in 2026, maintaining 
this momentum in subsequent years.
Finally, we remain deeply aware that MB’s 
success today has been built on the trust and 
companionship of our shareholders, investors, 
partners, customers, and the entire MB Group 
team. On behalf of the Bank’s Board of Directors 
and Leadership Board, I sincerely acknowledge 
the contributions of all stakeholders and 
reaffirm our commitment to the strategic 
direction we have pursued. With clear vision 
and strong determination, MB will move forward 
into 2026 with even greater achievements, 
further advancing its position toward regional 
leadership.
Sincerely,

Business Lines and Locations
Business lines
Business 
locations
MB conducts all types of commercial banking activities as prescribed by law and the State 
Bank of Vietnam under Establishment and Operation License No. 03/GP-NHNN issued 
on 16 January 2026, including key business lines serving both individual and corporate 
customers such as: Capital mobilization activities; Credit extension activities; Payment and 
treasury services; and other products and services in accordance with applicable laws.
As of December 2025, in addition to the Head Office, MB’s network comprised 
327 branches and transaction offices nationwide (an increase of 5 branches and 3 
transaction offices compared with 2024), one branch in Laos, and one public limited 
bank – MB Cambodia Public Limited Bank. In Vietnam, MB’s network covered 33 
of 34 provinces and cities, strategically located in key, high-potential, and densely 
populated economic regions to meet the growing demand for banking services from 
businesses and individuals. 
All MB branches and transaction offices were designed with open, modern spaces 
that meet international standards, offering maximum convenience for customers. 
Alongside the physical network, MB customers could access nearly all banking 
services through digital channels – enabling service anytime, anywhere. At each 
service point, MB staff have been professionally trained and dedicated to delivering 
personalized experiences, helping MB become the most convenient and trusted 
choice for all customer segments. MB’s network has consistently been recognized as 
one of the most efficient in the banking industry, offering a wide range of high-quality 
products and services while ensuring top-tier safety and security standards. With 
over 35 million customers, MB has remained a preferred financial destination across 
its operational areas. 
MB has affirmed its position among the Top 5 largest banks in Vietnam with 
impressive market share growth and outstanding growth rate of approximately 40%,

MB follows a corporate governance model in compliance with the provisions of Enterprise Law 
No. 59/2020/QH14, issued on June 17, 2020, under Article 137, Clause 1a, and the Law on Credit 
Institutions (2024). The governance structure includes General Shareholders Meeting (GSM), 
Board of Directors (BOD), Supervisory Board (SB), and Chief Executive Officer (CEO).
Organizational structure enhancements:
In 2025, MB refined its organizational structure and the functions of various units to better 
align with the practical requirements of business operations and execution, thereby optimizing 
governance efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.Accordingly, the Business Divisions 
strengthened segment-based management, with a focus on customer behavior insights and 
delivering products and services to Retail and SME customers along the customer journey.
The Data Division was also redesigned to centralize enterprise-wide data provisioning, optimize 
service level agreements (SLAs) for product delivery, enhance customer experience, and improve 
the quality of data-driven decision-making across the Bank.

Following the issuance of regulations related to operational risk management, MB conducted 
extensive and in-depth communication and implementation across all units and employees 
within the Bank to ensure a clear and comprehensive understanding of the Leadership Board’s 
risk management orientation; the roles and responsibilities of each unit and individual; the 
tools and methods for managing operational risk; as well as the operational risk appetite and 
limits that must be monitored and complied with.
In addition, recognizing that insurance can serve as a supplementary risk mitigation tool 
by providing financial compensation in the event of operational risk losses, alongside 
proactive preventive measures (particularly for objective risks arising from external causes), 
MB has purchased insurance coverage for several types of risks. These include insurance 
for cash in vaults, insurance for cash in transit, fire and explosion insurance, insurance for 
ATM vandalism, insurance for customer card skimming incidents, insurance for cases of 
loss of funds in accounts and cards related to fraudulent electronic communications, and 
cybersecurity insurance covering data asset losses and business interruptions.

from financial crimes, particularly those involving high technology and the Internet, such as 
online fraud, cyberattacks, and money laundering via digital currencies. In 2025, MB fully 
applied the methodologies delivered under the Financial Crime Risk Management project,

At MB, the BOD and the Leadership Board highly recognize the importance and necessity 
of Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing, Counter-Proliferation Financing, 
and Sanctions Compliance activities. Accordingly, they consistently devote close attention, 
investment, and strict supervision to the development and implementation of AML/CFT/
CPF and Sanctions Compliance measures.
AML/CTF efforts at MB are implemented based on the following principles: (1) Compliance 
with legal and MB regulations while ensuring national sovereignty and security, maintaining 
normal economic and investment activities, protecting the legitimate rights and interests 
of organizations and individuals, and preventing the abuse of AML/CTF/PF/Sanctions 
Compliance measures for improper purposes; (2) AML/CTF/PF/Sanctions Compliance 
measures must be executed comprehensively and timely, and any violations must be 
strictly handled.
MB defines key AML/CTF objectives as follows: (1) Ensuring MB’s compliance with legal 
regulations and alignment with international practices; (2) Preventing MB’s business 
channels, products, and services from being exploited as tools for money laundering, 
terrorism financing, proliferation financing, and sanctions violations; (3) Protecting MB’s 
reputation and credibility among customers and partners while mitigating potential 
financial losses.

Shinsei Finance Limited Liability Company (Mcredit), MB Cambodia Public Limited Bank, 
and MB Bank Vietnam (MBV) – MB mandates that its subsidiaries adhere to the parent 
company’s AML/CTF principles, ensuring a unified approach across the MB Group.
To achieve these objectives, the BOD and BOM acknowledge that AML/CTF implementation 
within each financial institution significantly impacts national and global AML/CTF 
efforts. This awareness has been effectively communicated to MB’s staff, employees, and 
subsidiaries, fostering a strong AML/CTF culture throughout the Bank and leading to more 
consistent, thorough, and effective execution of AML/CTF measures.
AML activities are structured around two key pillars: Know Your Customer (KYC) and 
Transaction Monitoring. The KYC process, including data collection, verification, periodic 
updates, and risk classification, is meticulously and continuously conducted by MB’s 
customer management branches. Transaction monitoring is performed before, during, 
and after transactions to detect and reject transactions outside MB’s acceptable policy 
framework, while continuously flagging suspicious cases involving potential money-
laundering activity. The effectiveness of AML execution is significantly enhanced by 
equipping staff and employees with the necessary tools. Accordingly, MB’s AML system, 
supplied by a leading global partner (Oracle), includes comprehensive components for 
Customer Due Diligence throughout the customer relationship lifecycle and transaction 
monitoring against sanctions/blacklists/warning lists. The system also employs scenario-
based transaction analysis to swiftly and effectively manage risks of money laundering, 
terrorism financing, proliferation financing, and sanctions violations, aligning with 
international best practices.

Environmental

Management
Adoption of 
International Best 
Practices:
To enhance transparency in the criteria for selecting projects or loans that meet green standards, 
MB developed the Green Credit Framework (2025), aligned with international capital market 
practices and relevant global agreements, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development 
Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. Through these regulations, MB 
established detailed taxonomy and specific technical criteria for projects across different green 
sectors, serving as the basis for assessing and appraising the environmental and climate benefits 
generated by projects or loans.
MB’s green credit framework was independently reviewed by KPMG India, one of the world’s leading 
independent audit organizations, which provided a Second Party Opinion (SPO) confirming that 
the framework complies with four core components in accordance with international standards: 
(i) Use of proceeds; (ii) Project evaluation and selection process; (iii) Management of loan proceeds; 
and (iv) Impact reporting. During 2025, MB also accelerated the growth of green credit within its 
credit portfolio in line with the SBV’s orientation. As of December 31, 2025, MB’s outstanding green 
credit balance exceeded VND 68 trillion, of which 80% was allocated to renewable and clean 
energy sectors, 11% to sustainable green agriculture and forestry, and 2% to sustainable water 
management.
To effectively manage the portfolio and promote sustainable finance growth, MB strengthened 
its human resources, systems, and internal capacity through training and capability development 
programs. The Bank will continue developing specialized financial products and programs to 
further promote green finance.
Recognizing the profound impacts of climate change and environmental pollution on the global 
economy and human life, MB has been actively developing and implementing environmental 
risk management practices within its credit activities to minimize negative impacts and advance 
its green and sustainable credit growth objectives. Currently, 100% of credit proposals are 
screened and classified based on environmental risk levels in accordance with Circular No. 
17/2022/TT-NHNN. For projects with identified environmental risks, the Bank requires customers 
to develop and commit to implementing Environmental and Social Action Plans (ESAP), which 
are incorporated into credit agreements as binding conditions for credit approval. MB is also 
moving toward implementing an ESG risk scoring system to enable more comprehensive risk 
identification and to align its practices more closely with international standards.
In 2025, MB received independent validation results from PwC confirming the Bank’s completion 
of Basel III implementation in accordance with international standards and its application in 
banking operations. 
Continuing a journey spanning more than a decade of persistent efforts to enhance risk 
management capacity in line with international standards, MB pioneered the research and 
implementation of Basel II as early as 2012, when the domestic regulatory framework had 
not yet mandated its adoption. During the period 2012-2021, MB continuously improved its 
risk management model, developed data infrastructure, and established comprehensive risk 
measurement systems, becoming one of the first banks in Vietnam to receive independent 
validation of its Basel II implementation from a reputable international audit firm. This 
achievement not only reaffirmed MB’s determination and execution capability in complying 
with international standards but also reflected the Bank’s long-term vision for sustainable 
development, proactively aligning with advanced governance standards and establishing a 
solid foundation for the early adoption and integration of Basel III outcomes into the Bank’s 
strategic development and operational activities.
Against the backdrop of Vietnam’s banking system’s progressive integration with international 
financial standards, MB continued to demonstrate its pioneering role by officially completing 
the validation project for the implementation of Basel III. The project was carried out in 
collaboration with the independent audit firm PwC to comprehensively validate the calculation 
results for capital adequacy ratios, liquidity indicators, and a stable funding structure under the 
Basel III framework.
The project included the assessment and validation of key components, including the Capital 
Adequacy Ratio (CAR), the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), and the Net Stable Funding Ratio 
(NSFR). These three indicators are the core pillars of Basel III – the global capital and liquidity 
standards designed to strengthen financial resilience and enhance the stability of the global 
banking system. Completion of the independent validation by an international organization 
not only reinforced MB’s credibility on transparency and compliance but also demonstrated 
the maturity of the Bank’s risk governance framework, capital management model, and 
internal supervision mechanisms.

The year 2025 marked the completion of the DC 5.0 Project, affirming that MB’s debt 
management and recovery practices have approached international standards and 
successfully integrated data and analytical models into the debt recovery process, thereby 
delivering sustainable value for both the Bank and its customers.
In 2025, MB finalized a debt recovery strategy for each customer segment across the 
delinquency lifecycle, based on data and analytical models. An automated, continuous 
monitoring mechanism was established to ensure effective implementation, enabling timely 
evaluation and updates to optimal recovery strategies. In parallel, the project continuously 
researched and deployed automation policies to process a large volume of small-value debts 
at optimized costs, thereby allowing resources to be concentrated on more complex and 
higher-value cases.
From an operational perspective, the organizational model clearly defined the roles between 
MB – Thinker and the debt collection units – Doer. A close coordination mechanism and 
frequent information exchange between field specialists and MB’s internal analytics and 
modeling teams were established to effectively leverage data, enhance analytical capabilities, 
and develop policies aligned with practical operational needs.
From a system perspective, the DC software platform was fully launched and deployed, 
covering the entire process from early-stage delinquency management to the handling of 
complex resolution options at later stages. The system was built on a comprehensive data 
foundation and integrated seamlessly with related systems, ensuring in-depth customer 
management capabilities and providing effective tools for debt recovery officers. MB is proud 
to be among the few banks in Vietnam pioneering comprehensive end-to-end automation of 
the debt recovery system.
With these foundations in place, debt recovery resources were optimized while operational 
efficiency continued to improve significantly. One hundred percent of retail debt cases were 
automatically assigned daily, and performance was continuously measured at a detailed level 
for each officer, segment, and stage of the recovery process. This represents an important 
milestone in the digital transformation of MB’s debt recovery operations, establishing a solid 
foundation for the Bank’s safe and sustainable growth in the coming years.

As of the end of 2025, MB’s total credit balance reached VND 1,110 trillion, maintaining 
a high CAGR of 35% over the past three years. In 2025 alone, credit grew by 37%, 
reflecting the Bank’s strong expansion capacity and its effective ability to meet the 
economy’s capital demands, with customer loans continuing to play the central role.
The credit portfolio recorded outstanding growth in the corporate customer segment, 
which increased by 45% in 2025 and accounted for 55% of total outstanding loans. 
This result demonstrates the Bank’s proactive approach in capturing opportunities 
from financially sound enterprises with strong competitiveness and high adaptability 
amid a still-challenging economic environment.
For the retail segment, the rate in the loan portfolio saw a slight adjustment 
downward in 2025. Nevertheless, the Bank’s Leadership Board continues affirming 
retail banking as a long-term strategic priority. Focusing on expanding lending to 
large corporates with strong financial capacity, while accelerating ecosystem-
based customer development, is considered a strategic move in line with a volatile 
economic landscape. This orientation not only supports risk control but also lays a 
solid foundation for sustainable growth and expanded business opportunities in the 
upcoming years.
MB’s non-performing loan (NPL) ratio continued to be tightly controlled at 1.3% as of 
the end of 2025, a significant improvement from 1.6% in 2024. This result reflects the 
effectiveness of the Bank’s risk management practices, credit appraisal processes, and 
post-disbursement monitoring, despite a challenging macroeconomic environment. 
To this extent, the Bank not only maintained asset quality within a safe threshold 
but also exceeded the target set by the General Shareholders Meeting (below 1.7%). 
The improvement in the NPL ratio has strengthened the Bank’s financial foundation, 
enhanced its risk resilience, and created additional room for sustainable credit growth 
in the upcoming periods.

Fee-based income 
In 2025, the Bank’s total operating income reached VND 67.7 trillion, representing a 22% 
increase compared to 2024. This reflects strong growth momentum and effective expansion 
of business scale, along with revenue optimization. Of this, net fee and commission income 
amounted to approx. VND 6.6 trillion, marking an impressive 51% growth, driven primarily 
by contributions from Insurance, Payment Services, and Treasury Operations.
Net fee-based income in 2025 reached VND 6.6 trillion with strong acceleration in 
2025, in which cash management and insurance services remained the primary revenue 
contributors, accounting for nearly 80% of total fee income. 
Detailed breakdown of fee revenue: insurance fee revenue exceeded VND 9.3 trillion, 
growing 11%; payment and cash management income of nearly VND 4.6 trillion, increasing 
37%; securities brokerage income reached VND 923 billion, up 47%. Advisory service 
income surged by over 257%, reaching more than VND 1 trillion. Debt handling, asset 
valuation, and asset exploitation income decreased 14% to over VND 427 billion. Other fee 
income grew 30% to nearly VND 1.8 trillion. 
Regarding expenses, insurance costs exceeded VND 6.3 trillion, slightly growing 2%; 
payment and cash management expenses reached over VND 2.7 trillion, up 19%; brokerage 
commission expenses surpassed VND 1.6 trillion, up 61%; expenses for debt handling, 
valuation, and asset exploitation amounted to nearly VND 327 billion, down 26%; securities 
brokerage expenses reached VND 226 billion, up 37%; expenses for entrusted operations 
and agency services exceeded VND 22 billion, up 27%; other service expenses stood at 
nearly VND 224 billion, up by more than 82% compared to 2024.

The global economy in 2026 is forecast to continue facing many risks, including slow growth, 
prolonged geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation, and supply chain fluctuations. These 
factors can negatively affect international exports, investment, and capital flows, thereby 
putting pressure on Vietnam’s macroeconomic stability in a highly open economy. In its 
January 2026 report, the IMF projected that global GDP growth in 2026 would remain 
unchanged from 2025 at 3.3%. Among them, developed economies are expected to grow 
by 1.8%, while emerging markets are projected to expand by 4.2%. Global inflation is 
projected to decline from 4.2% in 2025 to 3.8% in 2026 (Image 1 and Image 2).
2026 is the first year of implementing the 5-Year Socio-Economic Development Plan 
2026-2030, meaning the beginning and shaping of a whole new development cycle. 
Based on the positive results of 2025, Vietnam’s economy enters 2026 with many 
development opportunities but also faces many challenges from the domestic and 
international context. The economic outlook in 2026 is therefore both positive and 
requires prudence in management. In this context, Vietnam’s economy in 2026 is 
projected to grow by over 10%, with inflation at approximately 4.5-5%. Key growth 
drivers include industrial production, retail, and consumption, as well as continued 
growth in exports and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows.

The USD/VND exchange rate in 2026 is forecast to increase by 3-4%. Exchange rate pressure 
in 2026 is forecast to be lower than in 2025. The most important reason is the narrowing 
of the interest rate spread between VND and USD. Since the latter part of 2025, domestic 
interest rates have gradually increased, while USD interest rates in the international market 
remain in a downward trend. This development reduces the incentive to hold USD and 
shifts short-term capital out of VND, thereby easing pressure on the exchange rate relative 
to 2025. In addition to interest rate factors, domestic fundamentals continue to play a 
supportive role in stabilizing the exchange rate. The trade balance is expected to maintain 
a surplus, FDI disbursements are stable, remittances are sustainable, and international 
tourists will provide a regular source of foreign currency for the economy, giving the State 
Bank of Vietnam room to regulate the foreign exchange market more flexibly.
The macroeconomic environment, characterized by both opportunities and challenges, 
places the banking sector at the center, playing a strategic role in the economy’s 
development in the coming period. In 2026, the State Bank of Vietnam is expected 
to continue proactively and flexibly managing monetary policy, closely coordinating 
with fiscal policy and other policies to ensure system safety and liquidity, contribute to 
macroeconomic stability, control inflation, maintain economic balances, and create 
momentum for rapid and sustainable development.
Credit growth in 2026 is projected at around 15%, with non-performing loans (NPLs) 
expected to be controlled below 2%. At the same time, credit expansion will be directed 
toward production and business activities, while lending to the real estate sector will be 
strictly monitored and controlled. In 2026, interest rates in Vietnam may inch up slightly 
due to rising investment credit demand, but they will remain strictly controlled by the 
State Bank of Vietnam. The governing focus of monetary policy remains on maintaining a 
balance between supporting economic growth and ensuring macro stability, especially by 
stabilizing the exchange rate and the banking system.

Under the close guidance and clear strategic direction of the BOD, MB continued to make

MB achieved the following key milestones:
MB maintained a stable and prudent growth trajectory, meeting and exceeding many key 
targets set out in the 2025 business plan approved by the GSM. Total assets surpassed VND 
1.6 quadrillion, more than double the level outlined in the plan approved by shareholders. 
Credit growth and the CASA ratio remained among the highest in the market, reflecting 
MB’s strong competitiveness across both retail and corporate banking segments. Asset 
quality remained well controlled, with non-performing loans maintained within regulatory 
thresholds and below the industry average.
In terms of operational efficiency, profit before tax remained among the highest in the 
banking sector, demonstrating MB’s strong capabilities in cost management, business 
portfolio optimization, and operational efficiency.
Alongside strong financial performance, MB continued to position itself as a pioneering 
bank in comprehensive ESG implementation. During the year, the Bank issued a full 
set of ESG policies, implemented a green credit framework, expanded its portfolio of 
sustainable finance products, and progressively integrated ESG considerations into 
governance, operations, and risk management. Green credit in 2025 accounted for 7% of 
total outstanding loans, among the highest ratios in the market, reaffirming MB’s strategic 
commitment to promoting green finance and sustainable development.
In 2025, MB launched Touch Account, enabling customers to use their payment accounts 
directly on Apple Pay and Google Pay. The service can be activated in just five steps and allows 
payments via Face ID or fingerprint authentication even when offline. This solution significantly 
promotes cashless payments and strengthens MB’s presence in the global payment ecosystem.

agents, while digital fundraising volume reached VND 1.4 trillion per day.

protection rate. Its technology infrastructure processes 37 million requests per day with a

30%. The active-active operating model ensures high system availability and scalability to 
support rapid growth.

24/7 disbursement and automated credit line renewals, helping reduce errors and improve 
operational efficiency. MB also continued to invest heavily in technology infrastructure, 
with total investment reaching VND 16.8 trillion during the 2015–2025 period. By the end

storage capacity, while IT personnel accounted for 11.9% of total staff.

strategic direction and comprehensive oversight of MB’s risk management framework, 
ensuring operations remained within established risk limits and progressively aligned with 
international best practices. MB accelerated its roadmap toward Basel III compliance, 
positioning itself among the pioneering banks implementing advanced capital, liquidity, 
and risk management standards.
Governance and management bodies—including the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board, 
the Board of Management, business divisions, and subsidiaries—conducted a comprehensive 
review of internal regulations to ensure alignment with the Law on Credit Institutions 2024 and

compliance and enhance the effectiveness of its internal control system.

The system processes approximately 37 million requests per day, enhancing the straight-
through processing ratio and reducing operational risks through intelligent control mechanisms 
such as auto-switching, multi-source risk checks (FRCM, SIMO), and smart routing. 
MB placed strong emphasis on improving service quality across its core platforms. The 
Bank deployed comprehensive financial protection solutions across the entire customer 
journey on MB App and BIZ MBBank, utilizing a multilayer protection strategy to detect 
and warn of potential risks. As a result, the customer protection rate reached approximately 
80%, while customer losses declined significantly, from around VND 20 billion per month to 
approximately VND 2.2 billion per month. 
MB accelerated the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across multiple areas of 
operation, aiming to build a sustainable, agile, and highly adaptive operating model in 
response to market dynamics. The deployment of AI enhanced service quality, improved 
consistency, and standardized the customer experience across all platforms. Through 
automation and process optimization, AI shortened processing time, improved labor 
productivity, and significantly optimized operating costs. As a result, MB’s cost-to-income 
ratio (CIR) reached approximately 25.23%, decreasing by 1.9% compared to 2024.
MB continued expanding the use of data-driven models to support business development. Real-
time lead management and opportunity identification solutions were deployed to help sales 
teams improve conversion rates, personalize customer engagement scenarios, and shorten 
interaction time. Real-time and event-based technology platforms were also implemented to 
deliver timely business insights and optimize operational efficiency. In addition, MB deployed 
systems to manage and trace data processing flows, ensuring data integrity across the Data 
Platform as information is stored and aggregated across multiple systems and layers. 
To support its digital strategy, MB continued building a flexible workforce for the digital era. 
The Bank now employs approximately 2,500 technology specialists and IT professionals, 
representing about 12% of the system’s total employees. MB places people at the center of its 
strategy, supported by comprehensive and innovative employee welfare policies that combine 
competitive financial benefits with a healthy working environment, clear career development 
pathways, and recognition of individual contributions. A key element of this strategy is the 
“three highs” commitment—high capability, high speed, and high performance— encouraging 
employees to achieve peak productivity and deliver results efficiently.

MB’s Sustainable Development 
Message
The report is prepared to present and disclose official information on MB’s strategic 
direction, objectives, and the implementation results of its sustainable development 
initiatives and action programs.
2025 marked a pivotal turning point for the global economy, as the world entered a 
period of profound structural transformation in which environmental, geopolitical, and 
economic challenges collectively reshaped the foundations of global development. Shifts 
in global trade, supply chains, and strategic competition among nations have reshaped 
the trajectory of globalization, with economic security emerging as a central priority. 
The global economy is transitioning from highly centralized supply chains to multiple 
regional hub structures, from purely free-trade frameworks to trade increasingly aligned 
with national strategic interests, and from cost- and profit-optimized operating models 
toward risk-optimized, resilience-focused systems designed to withstand global disruptions 
better. At the same time, environmental challenges and climate change have increasingly 
emerged as systematic material risks with significant implications for both the global 
economy and the financial system. Sustainable development is no longer a long-term 
goal but has become a critical prerequisite for ensuring economic stability and national 
resilience. Accordingly, global capital is rapidly shifting toward green-economy sectors, the 
energy transition, technological innovation, and data-driven governance. 
Amid the ongoing global economic restructuring, Vietnam has emerged as a standout 
performer, underpinned by a stable macroeconomic foundation. In 2025, GDP grew by 
8.02%, significantly exceeding international forecasts, while average inflation remained at 
3.31%, supporting production, exports, and investment. Total import-export turnover was 
estimated at USD 930 billion, and foreign direct investment into Vietnam was projected at 
USD 27.62 billion, the highest level in the past five years. Public investment and domestic 
consumption have served as the core drivers of growth, reducing overreliance on external 
factors and establishing a robust logistics foundation for Vietnam’s green and digital 
transformation agendas. Combined with deepening regional integration, these factors 
reinforce Vietnam’s strategic role in regional supply chains. The shift in global production 
and trade presented a significant opportunity for Vietnam to upgrade its growth model, 
moving from a cost-based advantage to a focus on quality, innovation, and sustainable 
development. However, these opportunities come with unprecedented challenges. Vietnam 
is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change and must also meet increasingly 
stringent environmental, governance, and transparency standards required by international 
markets. Sustainable development has evolved beyond a policy objective to become a 
key determinant of national competitiveness in the new economic era. Vietnam’s next 
phase of development will be shaped by three core drivers: the green economy, the digital 
economy, and the knowledge economy, aimed at strengthening resilience and enhancing 
the country’s capacity to adapt to global disruptions proactively.

Key sustainable development 
projects in 2025
In 2025, MB launched the project of ESG datamart development to advance its goal of 
strengthening the Bank’s maturity in sustainable development governance. The system 
is designed to standardize and harmonize methods for recording, measuring, and 
monitoring sustainability-related indicators across the organization, ensuring consistency, 
transparency, and data traceability. Establishing standardized data platforms provides 
a robust foundation for collecting, consolidating, and reporting ESG information. This 
framework supports two key objectives: enhancing the effectiveness of internal governance 
and meeting the market’s increasingly rigorous disclosure requirements.
Building on this data framework, MB will continue to refine and expand the ESG data 
platform in 2026. The Bank will enhance data utilization capabilities toward greater 
centralization and standardization, including strengthening data analytics capabilities 
and broadening the scope of data collection. These efforts are progressively aligned with 
international best practices in sustainability disclosure while strengthening governance 
capacity to meet the expectations of regulators, investors, and rating agencies.
This project represents a key milestone in MB’s sustainable development transformation 
roadmap and was completed in 2025. It establishes a comprehensive foundation for 
sustainability governance aligned with international standards and best practices. The 
project also strengthened modern governance principles and mechanisms while enhancing 
MB’s ESG maturity and industry positioning. Following the project’s completion, MB 
streamlined and reinforced sustainability-related roles and functions to optimize resources 
and ensure effective implementation in line with international practices while remaining 
aligned with Vietnam’s market context.
This project represents a collaboration between Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank 
(MB) and FPT Corporation to apply green technology to optimize operations and monitor 
environmental impacts.
Under this partnership, MB deployed VertZéro—an advanced technology platform 
developed by FPT—to establish a carbon emissions data infrastructure and digitize the 
monitoring and evaluation of environmental performance indicators across its operations. 
This initiative supports MB’s commitment to generating positive environmental impact and 
contributes to Vietnam’s national goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050
The ESG Risk Management Framework project was one of MB’s key initiatives in 2025 to 
strengthen the Bank’s sustainable governance capabilities and progressively integrate ESG 
considerations into its enterprise risk management system in line with leading international 
practices. Through this project, MB established a roadmap to enhance policies, processes, 
and organizational structures toward a more advanced risk management model, while 
clearly defining the roles and responsibilities of relevant units in coordinating and managing 
ESG-related risks across the organization.
The implementation of the ESG Risk Management Framework contributes to: (i) 
comprehensive management of ESG risks that may impact key existing risk categories 
such as credit risk, operational risk, liquidity risk, and reputational risk; (ii) integration of ESG 
risk management into the Bank’s overall risk governance framework, ensuring alignment 
between sustainability governance and enterprise risk management; and (iii) strengthening 
monitoring, control, and risk-informed decision-making capabilities, thereby enhancing the 
Bank’s resilience to climate-, environmental-, and social-related disruptions.

Analysis of the operating context and identification of material topics
•	 Assess and analyze the macroeconomic environment, as well as sustainability 
requirements and commitments at the regional, national, and international levels, 
together with overall trends in the banking industry
•	 Identify opportunities and challenges related to sustainable development within the 
industry that may impact MB’s value chain, and assess their implications for MB’s 
strategy and operations
•	 Determine the set of environmental, social, economic, and governance topics relevant 
to MB’s value chain
Assess the environmental, social, and economic impacts of the identified topics

to develop a list of material sustainability topics (materiality is determined based on the 
nature and magnitude of impacts, frequency, scope, duration, regulatory requirements, 
and stakeholder concerns, etc.)
•	 Assess the positive and negative impacts of the organization on the Environment, Society, 
and Economy across each sustainability topic, based on scale, scope, and irremediability 
(for negative impacts only)
•	 Engage stakeholders to assess the relative importance of each topic

In 2025, Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB) continued to identify anti-corruption 
as a key priority in governance and operations, closely aligned with the objective of 
sustainable, safe, and transparent development. Anti-corruption efforts at MB were 
implemented consistently across the Head Office and branches, in strict compliance with 
applicable laws, as well as directives from the Party, the State, the Ministry of National 
Defence, and the State Bank of Vietnam.
MB has established a Steering Committee for the Prevention and Control of Corruption, 
Misconduct, and Crime, along with sub-committees at its business units. The Bank also 
regularly reviews and strengthens the personnel structure of these committees to ensure 
their effective and seamless operation throughout the organization.
Ensuring the rights of bondholders (creditors):
MB has issued a Corporate Bond Documentation Framework, which governs all activities 
related to bond issuance and trading at MB. This framework has been developed in 
compliance with the Law on Credit Institutions 2024, the Securities Law 2024, and relevant 
regulatory guidelines issued by competent authorities.
Prior to each bond issuance, all terms and conditions are fully and transparently disclosed, 
including: the Bank’s financial position based on audited financial statements, financial 
safety ratios, plans for fund allocation and payment of bond principal and interest, as well 
as the rights and obligations of bondholders, the Issuer, and other relevant parties. These 
are comprehensively detailed in the information disclosure documents.
MB’s commitments to protecting bondholders’ interests include:
•	 Information disclosure commitment:
MB commits to providing full, accurate, and timely disclosures in accordance with legal 
regulations governing private bond offerings in the domestic market and international 
bond issuances, and assumes full legal responsibility for the content and accuracy of 
disclosed information.
•	 Commitments to bondholders: 
+ Ensure full and timely payment of bond principal and interest upon maturity
+ Comply with regulations on the use of proceeds from bond issuances
+ Maintain the validity of all necessary approvals related to bond offerings
+ Comply with information disclosure requirements and other applicable regulations
+ Provide necessary information to bondholders in accordance with regulations
+ Ensure the rights and entitlements attached to the bonds for bondholders
+ Fulfill other obligations as specified in the disclosure document for each issuance
Other rights of Bondholders: 
•	 Each Bondholder shall be the sole owner of the Bonds and is entitled to receive full and timely 
payment of principal and interest; to receive all related payments, notices, and reports; and 
to enjoy other lawful rights associated with such Bonds in accordance with applicable laws 
and the provisions set out in the Information Memorandum of each issuance.
•	 Bondholders have the right to conduct Bond transactions in accordance with the 
Information Memorandum of each issuance and relevant legal regulations.
•	 Other rights shall be exercised in accordance with the Information Memorandum of 
each issuance and applicable laws. Bondholders are responsible for fully accessing 
and reviewing the Issuer’s disclosed information, clearly understanding the terms and 
conditions of the Bonds, as well as all provisions in the Information Memorandum and 
other commitments of the Issuer prior to making any investment or transaction decisions.

MB is always ready to proactively report, provide information, and closely coordinate with

damage. 
MB regularly communicates and disseminates directives issued by competent authorities 
and internal regulations related to the prevention and control of corruption, misconduct, 
and crime to all employees across the system. These documents are shared through the 
Bank’s internal network, enabling staff to review, update, and comply strictly with anti-
corruption requirements. 
In 2025, no cases of corruption-related violations involving MB employees were recorded. 
Employees across head office departments and business units clearly recognized their

codes of conduct, contributing to a transparent and open working environment.
At MB, complaint and denunciation handling channels have been established (at 
transaction points, via official correspondence, email, etc.), along with regulations and 
procedures for handling complaints and denunciations (information receipt – verification 
and processing – resolution and feedback), ensuring maximum convenience for customers, 
partners, and stakeholders. The regulations also clearly stipulate the confidentiality of 
whistleblowers’ identities and protection against retaliation.
In 2025, due to adverse impacts from socio-economic fluctuations and the increasing 
complexity of financial and banking transactions, the number of cases received and resolved 
by MB increased. The Bank’s leadership placed strong emphasis on handling customer 
complaints and feedback to enhance service quality and improve customer satisfaction 
with its products and services. Most customer inquiries related to clarifications and advisory 
on MB’s products and services. The main causes of complaints and denunciations arose 
from customers’ limited understanding of legal regulations, as well as the State Bank of 
Vietnam’s and MB’s internal policies and procedures (e.g., collateral handling, payment 
processes). MB strictly adhered to established complaint-handling procedures, ensuring 
prompt and timely resolution of all customer requests, with the following outcomes:
+ 100% of complaints and feedback were fully received and resolved in a timely manner, in 
compliance with legal regulations and ensuring customers’ legitimate interests. All handling 
results were duly reported to competent state authorities in accordance with regulations.

ESG Risk Management
With a customer portfolio spanning multiple industries and offering a wide range of credit 
products, MB adopts a balanced approach in integrating environmental and social risk 
management factors into the credit approval process for corporate clients. Based on the 
outcomes of the Project of ESG Risk Management Framework, MB is gradually establishing 
a comprehensive environmental and social risk management system, including internal 
regulations, processes, and implementation guidelines, as well as monitoring mechanisms 
aligned with Vietnamese regulations and international best practices. Currently, 100% of 
credit proposals within the applicable scope are screened and classified by environmental 
risk level in accordance with Circular No. 17/2022/TT-NHNN, enabling MB to determine 
appropriate environmental and social risk management measures corresponding to the 
identified risk levels. For projects where environmental risks remain, the Bank requires 
customers to develop and commit to implementing corrective action plans, which are 
recorded as conditions in the credit agreements.
Environmental and social risk management in lending activities is consistently considered 
in MB’s annual management orientation and integrated into the Bank’s overall risk 
management framework. In accordance with Circular No. 17/2022/TT-NHNN dated 
December 23, 2022, on environmental risk management in lending activities of credit 
institutions, MB has issued internal regulations to ensure risk control is implemented in line 
with the following principles:
•	 Investment projects must fully comply with legal regulations on environmental protection.
•	 TEnvironmental risk assessments must be conducted for each project/loan before 
making credit decisions.
To enhance the capacity to identify and manage environmental and social risks in lending 
activities, MB will pilot the ESG Scorecard tool in 2026, developed based on international 
advisory organizations’ references and tailored to align with the practices and specific 
characteristics of the Vietnamese market. The ESG Scorecard will support Relationship 
Managers (RMs) and relevant business units in identifying, assessing, and monitoring 
environmental and social risk factors related to credit risk, thereby improving the quality of 
credit appraisal and portfolio management.
In addition, MB is studying climate risk assessment methodologies aligned with advanced 
international practices to gradually assess the potential impacts of climate change on the 
Bank’s credit portfolio and operations, thereby strengthening its risk management capacity 
as it transitions to a low-carbon economy. 
The gradual adoption of ESG and climate risk assessment tools forms an important 
foundation for MB to enhance the resilience of its credit portfolio against long-term risks 
associated with climate change and the transition to a green economy.

partners, and community members.
In Spratly, the islands organized tree-planting and maintenance in accordance with 
approved plans. The Naval Region 4 Command received more than 340,000 trees from 
sponsoring organizations, localities, and enterprises, of which over 200,000 trees were 
planted in 2025.
The program not only improves the ecological environment in Spratly but also fosters a 
stronger sense of responsibility toward the nation’s seas and islands across the community.
Charity Platform:
Digital Infrastructure Connecting 
Social Resources
In 2025, the Digital Charity Platform continued to affirm its role as a digital infrastructure 
connecting social resources for community programs, with total donations reaching 
approximately VND 1,660 billion and 3.75 million transactions.
The platform was used to implement a number of large-scale campaigns both domestically 
and internationally, notably including:
•	 The campaign supporting the Cuban people titled “65 Years of Vietnam–Cuba Solidarity”, 
which mobilized more than VND 657 billion with 2.1 million contributions, creating strong 
community engagement and receiving positive recognition both domestically and 
internationally.
•	 Programs implemented in collaboration with the Vietnam Association of the Elderly, the 
Vietnam Association for Victims of Agent Orange/Dioxin, and the Vietnam Association 
for Supporting Families of Martyrs, aimed at honoring individuals who rendered services 
to the nation and supporting vulnerable groups.
•	 Disaster relief and emergency support programs for affected communities in various 
localities, implemented through the VNeID application, enabling rapid connection 
between the goodwill of people nationwide and affected areas, thereby ensuring that 
relief activities were conducted in a coordinated, practical, and effective manner.
In the coming period, the Charity Platform will continue to be developed as a trusted digital 
tool supporting the Government, organizations, and communities in implementing social 
welfare programs in a transparent, efficient, and sustainable manner, contributing to the 
social pillar of MB’s ESG strategy.

Social Welfare Initiatives
In addition to community fundraising initiatives, MB has directly implemented numerous 
social welfare programs nationwide.
During the 2021–2025 period, MB constructed and renovated nearly 6,000 gratitude 
houses, comradeship houses, and Great Solidarity houses for policy beneficiaries facing 
difficult circumstances.
In 2025, notable programs included:
•	 The Great Solidarity House Program commemorates the 80th anniversary of the Vietnam 
People’s Army and the 35th anniversary of the All-People National Defense Festival.
•	 The program to eliminate temporary and dilapidated housing nationwide, constructing 
more than 3,300 houses with a total budget of over VND 300 billion.
These initiatives demonstrate MB’s long-term commitment to working alongside the 
Government and communities to build an inclusive and sustainable society.
World Summit Awards 2025
In 2025, the Digital Charity Platform won the World Summit Awards (WSA) in the 
Government & Citizen Engagement category.
The WSA is an international award launched in 2003 to recognize digital solutions 
contributing to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(UN SDGs). In the 2025 edition, more than 400 digital solutions from around the world were 
nominated, and 40 outstanding solutions were selected for recognition.
The recognition of the Digital Charity Platform highlights MB’s effective use of technology 
to connect social resources, enhance transparency, and improve the effectiveness of 
community program implementation.
Community Drinking 
Water Initiative
The Community Drinking Water initiative is a community program designed to spread the 
spirit of the HiGreen Truong Sa campaign and encourage a greener lifestyle.
The initiative deploys a system of direct drinking-water dispensers using Japanese filtration 
technology at MB transaction points, providing clean, safe drinking water for customers 
and the public. The equipment does not generate wastewater, thereby contributing to 
reducing plastic waste and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
With more than 300 branches and transaction offices nationwide, MB’s service locations 
are not only places providing financial services but also spaces that connect communities 
and promote sustainable development values.

Digital Transformation 
Foundation
Cybersecurity, Digital Transformation, and Data Governance
Key Activities in 2025
For customer services provided at transaction counters, MBBank applies advanced 
technologies such as OCR, Intelligent Document Processing, and App Teller. These solutions 
enable MB staff to conduct electronic identity verification (eKYC) and collect customer 
information via NFC, ensuring a consistent customer experience, reducing processing 
time, and maintaining high standards of security and confidentiality. Technology adoption 
also allows the sales force to operate entirely through mobile applications when serving 
customers and distributing products. In addition, MB integrates banking services into 
partners’ digital platforms (such as e-wallets, e-commerce platforms, and ride-hailing 
applications) to create a convenient ecosystem and expand customer access channels. 
MB also accelerates the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning 
(ML), including: (i) Chatbots and virtual assistants: providing 24/7 support, answering 
customer inquiries, guiding transactions, and reducing call center workload; (ii) Product 
personalization: analyzing customer behavioral data to offer financial products and 
services tailored to specific needs; (iii) Biometric technology: applying facial recognition, 
fingerprint, and iris recognition for transaction authentication and electronic account 
opening (eKYC), thereby enhancing security and convenience; (iv) Big Data analytics: 
collecting and analyzing large volumes of customer data to better understand customer 
needs and behaviors, thereby optimizing marketing strategies and product development.
In governance and operations: MB applies information technology to optimize internal 
processes, enhance operational efficiency, and support decision-making: (i) Customer 
Relationship Management (CRM) systems automate internal management processes 
and customer information management, enabling more effective coordination among 
departments and improving service quality; (ii) Robotic Process Automation (RPA) 
automates repetitive tasks such as data entry and data reconciliation, helping save time 
and minimize errors; (iii) Cloud computing provides flexible infrastructure, rapid scalability, 
and reduced operational costs for banking systems; (iv) Data analytics and Business 
Intelligence (BI) provide reports and visual analytical tools to support the Leadership Board 
in making data-driven strategic decisions; and (v) 100% of employees use personal digital 
signatures, more than 30% of non-confidential documents are processed using end-to-
end personal digital signatures, 70% of regular meetings at the Bank are conducted online, 
and 80% of internal competitions and assessments with multiple-choice testing content 
are conducted via software platforms.
In risk management: MB applies information technology to identify, measure, control, and 
mitigate risks in banking operations: (i) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) 
analyze transactions in real time to detect abnormal behavioral patterns, enabling timely 
warnings and the prevention of fraud, anti-money laundering (AML), and counter-terrorism 
financing (CFT), while also supporting credit risk assessment through the analysis of credit 
scores, transaction history, and non-traditional data sources (such as telecommunications 
or social media data) to evaluate customers’ repayment capacity more accurately and 
efficiently; (ii) Big Data aggregates and analyzes data from multiple sources to build 
comprehensive risk profiles for customers and transactions; and (iii) information security 
and cybersecurity involve the deployment of advanced security solutions, including firewall 
systems, data encryption technologies, DDoS protection solutions, and Security Operations 
Centers (SOC), to safeguard customer data and banking systems against cybersecurity 
threats.

responsibilities in accordance with applicable laws, the MB’s Charter, internal governance 
regulations, and other relevant operational regulations. The Board’s activities were 
conducted regularly and closely aligned with the strategic orientations approved by the 
GSM, thereby enhancing governance effectiveness and improving operational quality 
across the entire system.

documents and records were properly maintained to ensure transparency and compliance 
throughout each stage.

The orientation for 
the implementation 
of the strategy and 
business plan for the 
year 2025
In 2025, the BOD continued guiding the implementation of key initiatives and strategic 
projects under the 2022–2026 Strategy, aimed at realizing the goal of becoming “a Digital
Corporation, a Leading Financial Group.” The BOD promoted greater cooperation with 
shareholders and strategic partners, thereby supporting MB in strengthening its competitive 
capabilities and improving business efficiency.
In parallel with restructuring efforts to resolve non-performing loans, the BOD also 
focused on expanding strategic partnerships with key shareholders and both domestic 
and international partners. Cooperation agreements have been implemented to enhance 
competitiveness, expand the service ecosystem, and create added value for customers, 
partners, and the market.
The BOD also focused on directing the development and refinement of modern business 
models and advancing key digital platforms, thereby offering new utilities and conveniences 
to individual customers, corporate clients, and partners across the entire ecosystem. These 
strategic orientations provide a solid foundation for MB to further enhance operational 
capacity, improve business performance, and promote sustainable development in the 
upcoming phase.

Reports of
the Independent Member of the BOD
The BOD for the 2024–2029 term (elected by the GSM on June 15, 2024) comprises 11 
members, including one Independent Member, while the remaining members are non-
executive, except for the Board Member concurrently serving as CEO, in compliance with 
applicable legal regulations. Mr. Luu Trung Thai was elected Chairman of the BOD, with 
three Vice Chairmen, including Ms. Nguyen Thi Hai Ly, Ms. Vu Thi Hai Phuong, and Mr. Vu 
Thanh Trung. The structure of the BOD was diverse, inheriting multiple generations, expertise, 
and multi-industry management experience. The BOD assigned responsibilities to its 
members based on their respective competencies, strengths, and experience, in which: The 
Chairman of the BOD is responsible for establishing the Board’s work programs and plans, 
allocating responsibilities among Board members, and directing the Group’s sustainable 
development initiatives; The Vice Chairpersons and Board members participate in the 
BOD’s committees and councils to provide advice and support to the BOD in performing 
its duties and exercising its authority in accordance with legal requirements.
In 2025, the Independent Member of the BOD actively participated in the Board’s programs 
and working sessions and served on the Risk Management Committee as assigned. The 
member contributed to the implementation of high-level supervisory responsibilities in 
relevant areas and promoted cooperation with strategic partners, aligned with his/her 
professional qualifications and strengths.
In addition to attending all periodic/ad-hoc meetings of the BOD and the Risk 
Management Committee, the Independent Member provided valuable input on important 
matters related to strategy, business planning, finance, investment, and senior personnel. 
The independent perspective and professional experience of the Independent Member 
contributed to enhancing the governance quality and strengthening oversight of the CEO 
and BOM.
The BOD for the 2024–2029 term quickly consolidated its organizational structure in 
accordance with good governance practices, while ensuring effective management and 
supporting sustainable development objectives. MB issued and amended its Charter, 
internal governance regulations, and other banking governance policies consistently in 
alignment with the resolutions of the GSM and newly enacted legal regulations.
BOD Committees and Councils (such as the Risk Management Committee, Human 
Resources Committee, Senior Management Committee, Technology and Digital 
Transformation Committee, and Group Coordination Council) operated in accordance 
with the regulations and provided advisory support to the BOD in the supervision and 
implementation of strategies.
The BOD held regular quarterly and ad hoc meetings and obtained written approvals 
to address matters within its authority; the Board members complied with the principles 
of meeting participation, discussion, and voting in the best interests of MB. Information 
disclosure and reporting to the GSM were carried out in a transparent manner in 
accordance with regulations.
With regard to oversight of the BOM, the BOD assigned specific members to supervise 
different areas of operation and to coordinate with the Risk Management Committee to 
provide governance guidance and identify and address potential risks at an early stage. 
The BOD also coordinated with the SB, inspection and audit authorities, and appointed 
an independent audit firm in the Big Four group in accordance with regulations (for 2024, 
KPMG was selected).
The supervisory results indicate that the management and operations of the CEO and 
BOM were conducted in accordance with the resolutions of the GSM, the direction of the 
BOD, and applicable laws; the BOD closely monitored operational developments, promptly 
identified emerging issues, and provided direction to the BOM for appropriate solutions. 
Transactions with internal persons and related personnel were conducted and disclosed in 
compliance with applicable laws and internal regulations.

operations of the Senior 
Management Committee
The Senior Management Committee continued to provide professional advice and 
recommendations to the Board of Directors (BOD) and the Chairman of the BOD on 
matters within the scope of the BOD’s authority and responsibilities. This committee also 
supported the BOD in timely handling key governance matters and overseeing the senior 
management team’s activities.

The Supervisory Board (SB) effectively completed the 2025 plan, fulfilling its oversight duties 
regarding business activities, corporate governance, management, the implementation of 
strategic initiatives, and other responsibilities in accordance with legal regulations, MB’s 
Charter, and resolutions of the GSM. The supervision was conducted comprehensively and 
in a timely manner, focusing on the following aspects: (i) Supervising MB’s operations and 
performance of its subsidiaries. in compliance with legal regulations/internal regulations/
Charter/resolutions of the GSM and Board of Directors (BOD); (ii) Supervising the activities 
of senior management; (iii) Monitoring the implementation of key projects, investment 
projects involving the purchase or sale of fixed assets, and contracts/transactions under the 
authority of the GSM/BOD; (iv) Supervising the financial position and appraising financial 
statements (FS) for 2024 and the first half of 2025 for MB; (v) Supervising risk management 
activities and compliance with the Law on Credit Institutions regarding limits to ensure 
safe banking operations; (vi) Supervising senior management’s oversight of Internal Audit 
(IA) in implementing the IA strategy for 2022–2026 and the 2025 plan. The oversight results 
showed that MB’s 2025 business performance generally met/outperformed the targets 
approved by the GSM, with key performance and scale indicators achieving solid growth 
compared to the market; MB’s FS provided a true and fair view of its financial position 
and business performance; MB complied with legal safety limits; Internal Audit completed 
its 2025 plan; Departments actively responded to and addressed recommendations from 
regulators, the SB, and IA. 
SB participated in/organized working programs/discussions with the independent auditor/
partners/experts from both domestic and international organizations to exchange/share 
best practices in corporate governance/management/digital transformation/control/
internal audit activities.
The SB effectively coordinated with the BOD, CEO, the BOM, and relevant units/individuals 
in carrying out its duties according to legal regulations and internal regulations as follows: 
•	 The SB aligned on mechanisms for supervision/coordination with the BOD/CEO/BOM/
related units/individuals (including shareholders) in implementing tasks as prescribed. 
Engaged in discussions and worked with the BOD/CEO/BOM on the annual control and 
internal audit plan. Worked with independent audit firms on the audit of MB’s FS. The 
BOD/CEO/ BOM/related units coordinated with the SB in the recruitment, appointment, 
dismissal, and rotation of Internal Audit personnel and implementation of strategic 
solutions of IA on digital transformation, creating favorable conditions for the SB to 
perform its functions and duties in accordance with the law, Charter, and other internal 
regulations.

of the BOD, and the BOM, and provided independent and objective opinions on 
contents/transactions under the authority of the BOD/Chairman of the BOD. At the 
same time, the SB provided opinions/advice to the BOD in approving decisions within its 
authority; consolidated the internal control system, implemented strategies, enhanced 
risk management capabilities, and improved the financial governance and operational 
efficiency of MB. The SB’s recommendations/advice were received by the BOD/CEO/
BOM, and related units were directed to implement them in good faith.

management, finance, business operations, strategy execution, and other responsibilities 
of MB, as well as the performance of subsidiaries in accordance with legal regulations, MB’s

At MB, the Internal Audit is a division-level unit, organized at the Head Office, under 
the SB and directly instructed by the SB, reporting directly to the SB in accordance with 
legal regulations and MB’s internal rules. As the third line of defense in the three lines 
of defense model, the Internal Audit conducts independent and objective reviews and 
assessments of the adequacy and compliance of mechanisms, policies, procedures, 
and internal regulations, then provides recommendations and advisory opinions 
to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of governance systems, processes, and 
regulations, thereby contributing to ensuring that MB operates safely, efficiently, and 
in compliance with applicable laws. 
In addition to its audit and advisory functions, the IA also performs a supporting 
and advisory role to the Supervisory Board, while assisting in the management 
and coordination of internal audit activities across the Group in accordance with 
applicable regulations.
At MB, compliance monitoring and supervision are carried out by units within the three 
lines of defense, with a unified scope to ensure no overlap. MB continues to align its 
monitoring with a broad-based approach and focused inspections, leveraging system-
based compliance supervision using technology-driven models and scenario-based alerts 
to detect early risk in line with MB’s digital transformation. 
In 2025, compliance monitoring and inspection activities were conducted in accordance 
with the approved plan. Risk-based inspections ensured comprehensive oversight across 
units, operations, and processes. The results showed that MB generally complied with legal 
regulations, SBV requirements, and internal regulations. Every finding was reported to the 
relevant units for the maximum resolution of identified violations. Every employee found to 
be in violation was handled in accordance with the rules (if applicable). 
In addition, to enhance the effectiveness of compliance management, MB strengthened 
the issuance of compliance risk bulletins and alerts to relevant units throughout 2025.
In 2026, in addition to continuing to expand the scope of inspection and monitoring and 
applying technology to these activities, MB will implement role-based compliance training 
programs and make them mandatory for certain positions, with the aim of fostering a 
proactive compliance culture across the organization.
The IA operates on the principles of independence, objectivity, conflict-of-interest 
control, and professionalism in accordance with applicable regulations. The IA 
ensures the independence in both organizational structure and operations; it 
is not subject to any interference or undue influence in the performance of its 
duties, the formulation of assessments, or the preparation of audit reports. 
Internal auditors do not concurrently undertake responsibilities under the first or 
second lines of defense, thereby ensuring a clear segregation of functions and 
preventing from conflicts of interest. All observations and conclusions in internal 
audit reports are carefully analyzed using data and information collected during 
the audit process, ensuring they are accurate, objective, and properly supported. 
In addition, internal auditors are required to meet all professional standards and 
ethical requirements in accordance with applicable regulations; comply with 
laws and MB’s internal regulations; and bear legal responsibility for the results of 
their assigned duties within the scope of their mandate.

In 2026, the Internal Audit will continue providing independent assurance and 
advisory services based on a risk-oriented approach, while strengthening data-driven 
continuous auditing and monitoring, further enhancing its advisory and early-warning 
role to the Leadership Board and the Supervisory Board, while ensuring that internal 
audit activities comply with applicable laws and adopt recognized best practices. 
The Internal Audit will also continue implementing and completing the initiatives and 
solutions under the Internal Audit Strategy for the 2022–2026 period, focusing on 
strengthening the internal audit system, planning and developing the Internal Audit 
data platform, and accelerating digital transformation and automation in internal 
audit activities, while further improving the audit risk assessment methodology and 
enhancing the quality of risk-based annual audit planning. The overall results of the 
Internal Audit Strategy for the 2022–2026 period will be comprehensively evaluated in 
2026, providing the foundation for developing the Internal Audit Strategy for the next 
phase, in alignment with MB’s development orientation and governance requirements 
under new circumstances.
The internal audit methodology is the “risk-based audit” approach, prioritizing 
resources to audit activities/units assessed as having high materiality/risk, 
ensuring alignment with the Bank’s risk appetite and governance requirements. 
Meanwhile, the IA progressively adopted modern audit methodologies and tools, 
such as Agile auditing and data-driven continuous auditing/monitoring, thereby 
enhancing flexibility, timeliness, and effectiveness in identifying, warning, and 
addressing risks, in line with MB’s digital transformation agenda and efforts to 
strengthen its governance capacity.
In 2025, the IA implemented its audit plan based on the results of its risk 
assessment, ensuring comprehensive coverage of key and high-risk areas 
across the Bank and its subsidiaries, while also fulfilling all tasks assigned by 
the Supervisory Board. The content and scope of audit, inspection, and review 
activities focused on assessing the effectiveness and efficiency of the internal 
control system; evaluating the performance and effectiveness of selected 
operations, units, customer portfolios, and products under audit sampling; 
conducting financial audits and reviews of financial statements; and assessing 
the compliance with applicable laws and internal regulations at the audited 
units and activities. In addition, the IA carried out advisory and consulting 
assignments at the request of the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board, and 
the Board of Management, and promptly implemented inspection and review 
requests from regulatory authorities. 
The quality of consulting continued to be maintained and promoted; audit results 
helped MB consolidate the internal control and risk management systems, and 
the SB’s recommendations/consultations were recognized, highly appreciated, 
and actively implemented by the management and units, contributing to 
revenue growth, cost optimization, and enhancing management and operational 
efficiency at MB.
